questions.question: When driving, keeping space between your vehicle and other vehicles is:
questions.explanation: Keeping space between your vehicle and other vehicles keeps everyone safe. If you need to stop quickly, this space gives you room to brake without hitting another vehicle.

questions.question: To confirm that a trailer has ABS, you can:

options.text: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors coming from the back of the brakes.
Look under the hood for the ABS sticker.
Remove a tire and look for the ABS sensor on the axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors coming from the back of the brakes.
questions.explanation: To check if a trailer has ABS, look under the vehicle for the electronic control unit and wheel speed sensor wires attached to the back of the brakes.

questions.question: What is a tire load?

options.text: The minimum safe weight a tire can carry
The maximum safe weight a tire can carry
The weight of the air within a fully inflated tire

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum safe weight a tire can carry
questions.explanation: Tire load is the heaviest weight a tire can safely carry at a specific air pressure. You can find this information on the side of the tire.

questions.question: When checking the air and electrical lines during a vehicle inspection, all of the following should be true, except:

options.text: The air hoses are making a hissing noise.
The air hoses and electrical lines are not cut.
The air lines are not pinched.
The air lines are not dragging against tractor parts.

questions.correctAnswerText: The air hoses are making a hissing noise.
questions.explanation: During your vehicle inspection, listen for leaks in the air hoses. The hoses and electrical lines should not be cut, worn, tangled, pinched, or dragging on any parts.

questions.question: What are placards?

options.text: Signs placed on a vehicle to identify cargo hazards
A type of tire used in snowy conditions

questions.correctAnswerText: Signs placed on a vehicle to identify cargo hazards
questions.explanation: Placards are diamond-shaped warning signs placed on vehicles carrying hazardous materials. They show what type of hazard is in the cargo.

questions.question: When conducting a vehicle inspection, you will need to identify all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: During your vehicle inspection, check the power steering belt, water pump belt, alternator belt, and air compressor belt. Look for cracks, frays, and proper tightness. Tell the examiner if any parts are not belt-driven and check that they work properly and are not damaged or leaking.

questions.question: After a vehicle is started, warning lights and buzzers:

options.text: Should stay on for several minutes.
Should turn off within a few seconds.
Should stay on until manually turned off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should turn off within a few seconds.
questions.explanation: After you start the engine, warning lights and buzzers should turn off quickly. If a light stays on, there is usually a problem with the vehicle.

questions.question: Emergency equipment, such as a fire extinguisher, is:

options.text: Only needed for vehicles transporting hazardous materials.

questions.explanation: All commercial motor vehicles must have emergency equipment. This includes spare fuses, three red reflective triangles or flares, and at least one working fire extinguisher.

questions.question: When performing a pre-trip inspection, you should make sure that:

options.text: The pedal surface has been smoothed out.
There is something underneath the brake pedal.

questions.explanation: When checking your pedals before driving, make sure nothing is blocking them. Check that the pedals work properly and have grooved surfaces if they should.

questions.question: If your vehicle is equipped with a cargo lift, you should ensure that:

options.text: The lift is the proper color.

questions.explanation: When checking a cargo lift, look for leaks, damage, and missing parts. The lift must be fully lowered and locked securely in place.

questions.question: If a driver feels tired while driving, what should they do?
questions.explanation: If you feel drowsy while driving, the only safe choice is to leave the road safely and sleep. Coffee and other stimulants are dangerous because you may crash when they wear off.

questions.question: When should you test the low pressure warning light?
questions.explanation: Your low pressure warning light must work properly. After the system charges, test it by quickly pressing and releasing the brake pedal. This releases air from the brakes. The warning light should turn on when pressure drops to an unsafe level.

questions.question: If a tire fails while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Loosen your grip on the steering wheel.
Check your tires after stopping completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your tires after stopping completely.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly if a tire fails. Do not use the brakes. Let the vehicle slow down on its own. Once it slows, brake very gently, pull off the road, and stop. Then check your tires.

questions.question: A registered vehicle must have:

options.text: A mirror on the left side only.
Mirrors on both the left and right sides.
A mirror on the right side only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Mirrors on both the left and right sides.
questions.explanation: Safe driving requires you to see all sides of your vehicle. You must have mirrors on both sides and check them regularly.

questions.question: When driving, where should you look?

options.text: Ahead, to the sides, and behind.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ahead, to the sides, and behind.
questions.explanation: Safe driving means being aware of everything around your vehicle. Watch the road ahead and check your mirrors often to see what is beside and behind you.

questions.question: If hydraulic brakes fail, how can you slow down?

options.text: Let the truck run out of gas.

questions.explanation: If your hydraulic brakes fail, shifting into a lower gear will help slow your vehicle down.

questions.question: How long after stopping on the road must you put out warning devices?
questions.explanation: Put out warning devices within 10 minutes of stopping on the road. Turn on your four-way emergency flashers when you pull over.

questions.question: What causes brake fade?
questions.explanation: When brakes are used too much, they overheat and work less effectively. This is called brake fade.

questions.question: A driver should always:

options.text: Drive faster than the speed limit.

questions.explanation: While driving, watch the road ahead for hazards. Plan what you will do if a hazard becomes dangerous.

questions.question: When carrying a wide load, what should you do?

options.text: Get special permits and follow special rules, such as driving at certain times.
Honk to make other drivers move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get special permits and follow special rules, such as driving at certain times.
questions.explanation: Wide loads need special permits. They can only be driven at certain times and may need special warning signs or equipment.

questions.question: Over-the-counter medication:

options.text: Is not covered by driving under the influence laws.
Can make it harder to drive safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can make it harder to drive safely.
questions.explanation: Over-the-counter and prescription medications can have side effects that reduce your ability to drive safely. It is illegal to drive while under the influence of alcohol or controlled substances, including some over-the-counter medications.

questions.question: An applicant will be denied a hazardous materials endorsement if they:
questions.explanation: Your hazardous materials endorsement can be denied or canceled if you are not a legal U.S. resident, you give up U.S. citizenship, you are wanted for or convicted of certain felonies, you are judged mentally incompetent or committed to a mental institution, or the Transportation Security Administration says you are a security risk.

questions.question: If involved in a crash, basic procedures should include all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: After a crash, you must protect the area, call the proper authorities, and help any injured people. Protecting the crash site helps prevent another crash in the same location.

questions.question: Trailers should:

options.text: Not be overloaded because it is dangerous.
Not be overloaded because drivers get paid only for certain weights.
Have all weight placed directly behind the cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not be overloaded because it is dangerous.
questions.explanation: Overloading a trailer is dangerous. It can damage the vehicle and make it harder for the driver to control.

questions.question: A vehicle inspection is required:
questions.explanation: State and federal laws require that commercial motor vehicle drivers inspect their vehicles before every trip.

questions.question: To get a hazardous materials endorsement, an applicant must provide:

options.text: A list of countries visited in the last 10 years.
Their job history for the last five years.

questions.explanation: To get a hazardous materials endorsement, you must provide your fingerprints and pass a Transportation Security Administration background check.

questions.question: Antifreeze helps keep an engine working properly:
questions.explanation: Your vehicle's cooling system needs enough water and antifreeze at all times. Despite its name, antifreeze is helpful in hot weather too.

questions.question: If another vehicle is tailgating you, you should:
questions.explanation: If you are being tailgated, create more space in front of your vehicle so the tailgater can pass safely. Speeding up will not help because the driver may tailgate you at the higher speed, making it more dangerous.

questions.question: If cargo on a flatbed trailer is 40 feet long, it needs a minimum of:
questions.explanation: On flatbed trailers and trailers without sides, cargo must be tied down. Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. No matter the cargo size, use at least two tie-downs.

questions.question: When driving through a curve on the skills test, you should:

options.text: Change lanes if needed to complete the curve.
Slow down after entering the curve.
Stop checking for other vehicles while turning.
Slow down before entering the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before entering the curve.
questions.explanation: Slow down enough before you enter a curve so you do not need to brake or shift while turning. Keep your vehicle in its lane and watch for traffic in all directions.

questions.question: What may cause someone to be denied a hazardous materials endorsement?

options.text: They are not a lawful permanent resident of the United States.
They had a speeding conviction in the last three years.
They did not answer every question correctly on the hazardous materials test.
They did not pass the hazardous materials test on their first try.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are not a lawful permanent resident of the United States.
questions.explanation: You will be denied a hazardous materials endorsement or lose an existing one if you renounce your U.S. citizenship, are not a lawful permanent resident, are wanted or convicted of certain felonies, are judged mentally defective, are committed to a mental institution, or are considered a security threat by the Transportation Security Administration (TSA).

questions.question: What are escape ramps?

options.text: Ramps to exit the interstate quickly.
Ramps that connect four-lane highways to two-lane highways.
Ramps that stop runaway vehicles on steep hills.
Ramps that cannot be used by automobiles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ramps that stop runaway vehicles on steep hills.
questions.explanation: Escape ramps are built on steep downhill sections to safely stop runaway vehicles. They have a long bed of loose, soft material and sometimes an uphill slope.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes, what pressure should be built up in both brake systems?
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes, allow time for the air compressor to build up at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems.

questions.question: After you stop during the stop/start maneuver, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the vehicle in first gear.

questions.explanation: When parking during the stop/start maneuver on a driving skills test, apply the parking brake. Shift into neutral or park. Park parallel to the curb and do not block any driveways or intersections.

questions.question: What can affect how far your vehicle travels before stopping?
questions.explanation: Stopping distance is affected by your vehicle's speed, its weight, and how much traction the road surface provides.

questions.question: Which is a good rule for making a turn?

options.text: Use your arms to get other drivers' attention.
Turn off your turn signal before entering the turn.

questions.explanation: Signal well before you turn so drivers behind you know your intentions. Keep the signal on during the turn and turn it off when the turn is complete.

questions.question: How do you check hydraulic brakes?

options.text: Pump the brakes three times, then press firmly for five seconds. The pedal should not move.
Pump the brakes three times, then press firmly for five seconds. The pedal should slowly move toward the floor.
Pump the brakes three times, then press firmly for five seconds. The pedal should slowly rise.
Pump the brakes three times, then press firmly for five seconds. The pedal should be easy to push to the floor.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pump the brakes three times, then press firmly for five seconds. The pedal should not move.
questions.explanation: To test hydraulic brakes, pump the pedal three times, then press firmly and hold for five seconds. The pedal should not move. If it does, there may be a leak.

questions.question: If you feel tired before driving, what should you do?

options.text: Drive as fast as possible to reach your destination quickly.

questions.explanation: Caffeine and other stimulants may keep you awake but will not make you more alert. Fatigue means your body needs sleep. The only real solution is to stop driving and get rest.

questions.question: How can you reduce the braking needed when going downhill?
questions.explanation: Shift to a lower gear before going downhill. This helps your vehicle maintain a safe speed without using the brakes too much.

questions.question: Why are roads especially slippery when rain first begins?

options.text: Water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
Gravel gets washed to the middle of the lane.
Tires are not designed for rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery when rain first begins. Fresh rainwater mixes with oil and grease on the road to create a slick film. As rain continues, this mixture eventually washes away.

questions.question: Emergency brakes are:

options.text: Only required when transporting hazardous materials.

questions.explanation: All trucks, truck tractors, and buses must have emergency brakes and parking brakes.

questions.question: It is illegal to operate a CMV with a blood alcohol content (BAC) of:
questions.explanation: Operating a CMV with a BAC of 0.04 percent or higher is illegal. A first offense results in losing your license for at least one year. If you have any alcohol in your system but stay below 0.04 percent, you will be taken out of service for at least 24 hours.

questions.question: Distracted driving:

options.text: Always comes from physical distraction, not mental distraction.
Can be increased by pre-programming radio stations.
Can be avoided by eating while driving.
Can be avoided by not having complex conversations while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be avoided by not having complex conversations while driving.
questions.explanation: To reduce distraction, avoid complex or emotional conversations while driving. Pre-program your radio before you start, and do not eat, drink, or smoke while driving. Mental distractions are as dangerous as physical distractions.

questions.question: When traveling with cargo, check it:

options.text: Before the trip and after the first 50 miles.
Only after arriving at the final destination.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before the trip and after the first 50 miles.
questions.explanation: Check cargo before you start, within the first 50 miles, and every three hours or 150 miles after that. The driver is responsible for keeping the cargo safely secured throughout the entire trip.

questions.question: When performing the stop/start maneuver during the skills test, you should:

options.text: Cut off other vehicles if needed to get onto the shoulder.
Slam on the brakes to stop as quickly as possible.

questions.explanation: During the skills test, you will pull over and stop as if checking your vehicle. Check traffic, use your turn signal, slow down gradually with smooth braking, change gears as needed, and come to a complete stop without coasting.

questions.question: Overloading cargo hurts all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Overloading a vehicle damages steering, braking, and speed control. Pay attention to how your vehicle handles when carrying extra weight.

questions.question: A truck may need to carry less than the legal maximum weight when driven on:
questions.explanation: In some driving conditions, it is not safe to operate a vehicle at full legal weight. Be careful in poor weather and on mountainous roads.

questions.question: A serious traffic violation includes all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Serious traffic violations include excessive speeding, reckless driving, operating a CMV without a valid CDL, following other vehicles too closely, and improper lane usage. Multiple serious violations can result in losing your license.

questions.question: Mirrors should be adjusted:

options.text: When you are standing next to the vehicle.

questions.explanation: Check mirrors before you start your trip. On a vehicle with a trailer, mirrors can only be adjusted correctly when the trailer is straight.

questions.question: When inspecting the exhaust system, which should not concern you?

options.text: Exhaust system parts that are not rubbing against fuel system parts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Exhaust system parts that are not rubbing against fuel system parts.
questions.explanation: When inspecting the exhaust system, watch for loose, broken, or missing pipes, mufflers, and tailpipes; loose or broken brackets, clamps, bolts, or nuts; exhaust parts rubbing against fuel system parts, tires, or other moving parts; and leaking exhaust system parts.
